newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Euro-Med countries pledge more cultural exchanges.
newsitem.headline: Euro-Med countries pledge more cultural exchanges.

text.p: A conference on cooperation between the European Union and Mediterranean countries recommended on Tuesday increased exchange programmes in the fields of education, sport and the arts.

The two-day talks on "Governance in the Euro-Mediterranean Region", an extension of the Euro-Med partnership launched in Barcelona in 1995, were hosted by the Netherlands as the EU president for the first half of 1997.
"We have focused our discussions especially on the work programme with respect to the partnership in social, cultural and human affairs," the conference's closing statement said.
Recommendations included an exchange programme for teachers, students and non-governmental organisations dealing with racism.
The statement said there should be exchanges in the field of public administration as well as sports and the arts.
It also called for the development of a Euro-Med television programme.
At a meeting in Tunis last year the countries drew up a draft plan in the economic sphere, which centred on industrial cooperation including gas and electricity projects.
The Hague meeting also welcomed the proposal of the Moroccan government to organise another Euro-Med conference in 1998.
